clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms: 'the effective date of article IX, section 4, be extended to July 1, 1934'. Recorded as 1934-07-01, the stated date on which the postponed provision takes effect and the postponement ends; the postponement ran through June 30, 1934, and an inclusive reading of the stated date would carry it through the end of July 1, 1934. Actor: EO 6467 itself. The later repeal of June 14, 1935 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) is a later event after the clause had expired. Own terms control. The order fixes July 1, 1934 as the date to which the effective date of Article IX, section 4 is extended; on that date the provision takes effect and the postponement has nothing left to postpone. The dossier's fixed-term own-terms record (TERM:record) states 1934-07-01. The end is recorded as 1934-07-01, the stated date; the postponement covered the days before that date (last postponed day June 30, 1934), and the alternative inclusive reading of the stated date would carry it through the end of July 1, 1934. The order's own 10-day proviso ('unless cause to the contrary shall have been shown to the Administrator') is a condition on its start; no held record shows cause was shown.

research_rationale:
EO 6467 (November 27, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) is read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6467-code-fair-competition-for-the-retail-trade-order-no-7-extension.txt; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; APP node 362290; wayback capture 2023-09-05T15:52:28Z). APP page check under AGENT_PROTOCOL.md: the MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl row with the same sha256 (36a085929dd7...) has heading 'Executive Order 6467—Code of Fair Competition for the Retail Trade, Order No. 7, Extension of Effective Date of Article IX, Section 4' and date 1933-11-27, the heading's number and subject and the date agree with the text (which ends 'The White House, ...' with the same date), and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's text_sha256 (d3000ab7eec6...). The text is complete (operative paragraph, signature, recommendation line and date). Identity: the census register (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) title 'Executive Order 6467—Code of Fair Competition for the Retail Trade, Order No. 7, Extension of Effective Date of Article IX, Section 4' dated 1933-11-27 and the WPA 1944 numbered-list summary 'Effectivedate of Article IX, Section 4, of Code of Fair Competition for the Retail Trade extended to July 1, 1934. III NRA Codes 660.' agree with the text. original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. Operative command: the order postpones the effective date of Article IX, section 4 of the Retail Trade code (the code approved October 21, 1933 by EO 6351): 'it is hereby ordered that the effective date of article IX, section 4, be extended to July 1, 1934, this order to become effective within 10 days of the date hereof unless cause to the contrary shall have been shown to the Administrator before that date.' Clause inventory: the machine inventory is accepted as complete (one clause, the operative paragraph with its signature and recommendation lines). First end: by its own terms on 1934-07-01, the date to which the order extends the effective date of Article IX, section 4; the later repeal (S.J. Res. 113, June 14, 1935) is a later event after the postponement had run. Effect on later law: none; the postponement had expired about eleven months before the repeal.

savings.reason: Acts and omissions while Article IX, section 4 was postponed are accrued; the postponement commanded nothing after July 1, 1934. From July 1, 1934 the provision operated as part of the Retail Trade code under its own terms, and its later fate belongs to the code approval (EO 6351), not to this order. The order's 10-day effectiveness proviso and the repeal of June 14, 1935 do not continue the postponement.
